name: Resign, serve the notice period, hand over everything held, and close the record cleanly on the leaving date
priorityReason: Nothing assigned to a leaver releases itself. Without the handover, periods go unstaffed and marks stay unsubmitted.

goal.capability: to resign from my own portal, serve my notice and hand over everything I hold
goal.outcome: I leave with my settlement paid and my letter issued, and the school is left with nothing unstaffed

postConditions: The resignation is on record with its reason, its approval and the leaving date the notice period produced.
Everything the employee held was reassigned to a named member of staff and ticked off, because none of it releases itself.
Marks outstanding for an exam in progress were either entered before the leaving date or transferred to whoever took the subject over.
The leaving date did not pass with anything unassigned, and anything outstanding was escalated to the Principal.
The employee stayed active on the roster through the notice period and continued to appear in attendance, leave and payroll.
On the last working day the login was revoked and the ID card and biometric enrolment cancelled, so neither the system nor the gate still admits them.
The final settlement was calculated — salary to the leaving date, unused leave entitlement, and any advance recovered or written off with approval.

The staff record was deactivated and not deleted, and the employee dropped out of payroll runs and out of the timetable.

businessRules.rule: The employee submits their own resignation from their own portal, with the reason and the date they wish to leave. Nobody resigns on somebody else's behalf.
The resignation goes to the School Admin. Whether the Principal must approve it as well is a configuration the Super Admin sets.
On approval the notice period starts. It defaults to the notice period on the staff record and can be changed, and the leaving date follows from it.
The employee is told the resignation is approved, the notice period and the leaving date it produces. A leaver who does not know their own last day cannot plan a handover.

On approval a handover checklist is produced listing everything assigned to that person, because none of it releases itself: every timetable slot they teach, any section they are in charge of, any exam subject with marks not yet submitted, and any activity they run. Each item is reassigned to a named member of staff and ticked off.

Marks outstanding for an exam in progress are either entered by the leaving employee before the leaving date or transferred to whoever takes the subject over, since the subject stays open and the exam cannot be locked without them.
The leaving date cannot pass with items still unassigned on the checklist.
The School Admin is warned as the leaving date approaches, and anything still outstanding is escalated to the Principal, so no period is left unstaffed.

The School Admin may change the length of the notice period at any point before it ends, or cancel it altogether. Cancelling withdraws the resignation and returns the employee to normal status, and the employee is told of either change.

Through the notice period the employee stays active on the roster and continues to appear in attendance, leave and payroll. On the last working day the login is revoked and the ID card and biometric enrolment are cancelled, so neither the system nor the gate still admits them.

Accounts calculate the final settlement: salary to the leaving date, any unused leave entitlement, and any advance still outstanding, which is either recovered from the settlement or written off with approval.
An experience or service letter is issued to the employee. The certificate module currently issues for students only and has to be extended to cover staff.
The staff record is deactivated and never deleted, because payroll history, ledger entries and audit trails all reference it. The employee drops out of payroll runs and out of the timetable.

basicFlow.userAction: Submits a resignation from their own portal with the reason and the date they wish to leave.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records it against their own record and routes it to the School Admin.
Routes it further to the Principal where the configuration requires it.

basicFlow.userAction: Starts the notice period, defaulted from the staff record and changeable here.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Sets the leaving date from the notice period and tells the employee both.
Lists every timetable slot they teach, any section they are in charge of, any exam subject with marks not submitted, and any activity they run.

basicFlow.userAction: Reassigns each item to a named member of staff and ticks it off.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Clears the item, and refuses to let the leaving date pass with anything unassigned.

basicFlow.userAction: Enters outstanding marks before the leaving date, or they are transferred to whoever takes the subject over.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Keeps the subject markable, since the exam cannot be locked without the marks.
Revokes the login and cancels the ID card and biometric enrolment on the last working day, having kept the employee active on the roster throughout the notice.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → HR → Final settlement → Calculate → Release
basicFlow.userAction: Calculates the settlement — salary to the leaving date, unused leave entitlement and any outstanding advance — and releases it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Recovers the advance from the settlement or writes it off with approval, issues the service letter, and deactivates the record.

alternateFlows.condition: The configuration requires the Principal's approval
alternateFlows.behaviour: It goes to the Principal as well as the School Admin, as the Super Admin has configured (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin rejects the resignation
alternateFlows.behaviour: The reason is recorded and the employee is told. No notice period starts and nothing is handed over.

alternateFlows.condition: The notice period is changed after it starts
alternateFlows.behaviour: The length is changed at any point before it ends, the leaving date moves with it, and the employee is told (BR-9).
Cancelling withdraws the resignation and returns the employee to normal status. The employee is told (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: Items are still unassigned as the leaving date approaches
alternateFlows.behaviour: The School Admin is warned and anything outstanding is escalated to the Principal, so no period is left unstaffed (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: An exam is in progress with marks not submitted
alternateFlows.behaviour: The responsibility passes to whoever takes the subject over, since the exam cannot be locked without the marks (BR-6).

alternateFlows.navigation: Final settlement → Recover advance, or Write off advance
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recovered from the settlement, or written off with approval. It does not lapse (BR-11).

departures.requirement: Every timetable slot, section, unsubmitted exam subject and activity the person holds appears on the checklist and must be reassigned to a named person. There is no bulk release and no automatic reassignment.
The exit cannot complete while any checklist item is unassigned, and outstanding items escalate rather than expiring.
The employee appears in attendance, leave and payroll throughout the notice period, and drops out only from the leaving date.
Login, ID card and biometric enrolment are all revoked on the leaving date, and a failure to revoke any of them is flagged rather than passing silently.
The staff record, the resignation, the handover and the settlement are retained 7 years after exit, since payroll and ledger history reference them.

The certificate module issues for students only and has to be extended to cover staff. When?
openQuestions.assumption: Not scheduled. A leaver currently cannot be given a service letter.

openQuestions.question: How is unused leave entitlement valued — at the daily rate, and over what period?
Who approves writing off an advance at exit?

openQuestions.question: May the settlement be released before the handover is complete, if the employee has already gone?
openQuestions.assumption: Not as modelled. The school would have no hold left.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
